name: Art Nouveau object
region: Brussels, Paris, Nancy, Vienna and Glasgow
summary: Lamps, glass, furniture and fixtures drawn from the line of a plant stem: cast bronze, art glass, carved fruit wood and porcelain, with one long curve that joins structure and ornament.

philosophy.core_thesis: An object grows like a plant: its structure and its ornament are one curved line, made by a craftsman from the best material.
design_principles: Draw each support as a plant stem that is thin at the root of the curve and thick where the load meets it.
Join structure and ornament in one S-shaped line; a leg, a handle and a leaf are one stroke.
Use coloured art glass in two to four layers for a shade or a vase, and let light pass through it.
Cast the metal parts in bronze or brass and give them a brown or green patina.
Carve fruit wood with a curved edge; leave 3 to 5 mm of soft radius on every corner.
Take the motif from nature: the iris, the orchid, the water lily, the dragonfly and the thistle.
Make each piece a unit with its room: the same curve runs on the lamp, the tap, the chair and the handle.
anti_patterns: Straight rods and sharp right angles
Machine-perfect chrome with no hand mark
Revival ornament, such as acanthus leaves or Gothic crockets
Flat colour with no depth in the glass

form.geometry: Whiplash curves, ellipses and drops; each form swells and narrows along one curved axis, as a stem or a bud does.
form.silhouette: An asymmetric outline with a long S-curve: a lamp stem bends to one side and ends in a bud-shaped shade.
form.edges: Soft edges with a radius of 3 to 10 mm; the rim of a vase and the edge of a table top flow in a wave, not a straight line.
form.proportion: A table lamp is about 45 cm high; the shade is 1 to 1.2 times the width of the base, and the stem is slim, about 1 part to 4 parts of height.
form.ornament: Plant and insect motifs in relief, in inlay or in the glass layers; they cover 30 to 60% of the surface and follow the structure.
rules: Each piece has one dominant curve that runs from the base to the top.
No part is a straight line longer than 15 cm.
Legs and stems are thin at the join and thick at the load, in a ratio of about 1 to 2.
Each motif follows the structure; no motif is a flat pattern that ignores the form.
Glass has 2 to 4 layers of colour; the outer layer is cut or etched to show the inner layer.

materials.rule: Glass and metal carry the light and the line; wood and textile are warm and dark, and each wood piece is about 40% of the visible surface.

finish.gloss: 30–70 GU on wood and patinated metal; 80–95 GU on glaze and glass
finish.patina: The style wants a brown or green patina on bronze and a deep, warm shine on wood; a bright new surface looks wrong.

hardware.section: Stems and rods 10–18 mm, narrowing to 6 mm; handles 12–20 mm
hardware.joints: Cast in one piece, or joined by a hidden dovetail or a tenon; a screw is hidden under a bud, a leaf or a cap.
hardware.handles: A cast bronze pull in the form of a stem, a tendril or a leaf, with a long curve that fits the hand.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A tap with a swan-neck spout and a lever in the form of a stem; a switch in porcelain or brass on a carved wood block.

palette.strategy: The soft, dim colours of a pond and a garden at dusk: moss, ochre, peach and aubergine, with warm metal and amber light.

processes: cameo glass cutting and acid etching
manufacture.scale: Art workshops and small factories made limited series of a few hundred; a few firms made larger series for the shop and the catalogue.
manufacture.signs: Cast seams that the chaser has worked away, a signature cut in the glass or the foot, and layers of colour at a cut edge.

objects.form: surface switch on a wood block
lead-glass shade on a cast base
round table on a central column

positive: whiplash curve and plant stem form
cameo art glass in layered colour
cast bronze with brown and green patina
swan-neck tap with a stem lever
studio product photograph, warm low light

canonical_works.work: Door handles and railings of the Castel Béranger

emotion.target_response: Quiet wonder at a handmade object that seems to grow: the viewer follows one line from the base to the top.

use_cases: lighting and glass for a period or reissue interior
a still life for an antiques catalogue
hardware schedules for a restored townhouse
a brief for a hand-finished reissue
avoid_when: The room needs plain geometry and no ornament.
The brief asks for chrome, plastic or a strict grid.

modifiers.how: Replace the curve with a stepped line and a fan, and use ebony, chrome and black glass.
Keep the craft, but use oak and hammered copper, with a straight line and a visible joint.
Remove the motif and the curve; use opal glass, nickel and plain solids.

era_blend.note: A new object that quotes the curve and the glass keeps the style.
